question: Should a traveller combine prayers by default, or pray each prayer on its time?
answer:
Now, one point though: jama' is allowed, but is it the mustahab thing to do? We said qasr is mustahab by unanimous consensus. Jama' is not mustahab. Jama' is khilaf al-awla — even in the other madhhabs; especially the Hanbali madhhab is very clear on this point. Jama' is not the default, and to not do jama', you will be rewarded. So the default: you do qasr, yes; you don't do jama'.

And I have to say — and may Allah forgive me, because I take too much laxity in this myself as well — when we do safar, we just take it as the default to do jama'. And **the default is you do qasr, but not jama': you pray every salah on its time.**

And Ibn Taymiyyah mentions this. He mentions many ahadith: all of these show that jama' is not from the Sunnah of traveling, unlike qasr. Rather, jama' is only done when there is a need to do so, regardless of whether one is traveling or not. Therefore, if the traveler needs to do jama', he may do so. For example, he's on the camel and he's going to have to stop the camel; it's an awkward inconvenience for this person — go ahead and do jama'. However, Ibn Taymiyyah says, as for the one who stops in a village or city for a few days, then his ruling becomes the ruling of the muqim — not for qasr, but for jama'. So he's going to pray dhuhr at its time — how many? Two, very good, you guys are following this — and asr at its time, and like that.

And Ibn al-Qayyim says that jama' is not a recommended Sunnah, in contrast to what the majority of musafirin think. So it's not just our generation; Ibn al-Qayyim also says this. The majority of musafirs, they get lazy, and they just think we should do jama'. Rather, jama' is the exception and not the rule. Regardless of whether one is traveling or not, one should pray salah at its time; that is the default ruling.

So when we are traveling — yes, on the side of the road you've got to stop over, understandably; you don't want to stop again — go ahead, do jama'. But once you get to the next city, once you are there temporarily, the default... Now, because you are a musafir, you are not sinful for doing jama', but it is khilaf al-awla. It is basically — call it makruh. You get reward for doing it on its time. Unlike qasr: you get reward for doing qasr, but for jama' you do not get reward. Actually, it's the opposite of that.
